aliases: Traktor Scratch Pro control vinyl MK2
summary: Native Instruments Traktor Scratch control vinyl MK2 (the owner's timecode record) for Traktor Scratch Pro / Traktor Pro; MK1 vinyl and the control CD are listed as secondary formats.
identityNotes: Confirmed by the owner: the control vinyl is Traktor Scratch Control Vinyl MK2. MK1 and the control CD stay listed as secondary formats (modern Traktor Pro reads both). MK2 carrier: Mixxx's Traktor MK2 work (PR 14569, DVS internals Pt. 3) and xwax list discussion give 2500 Hz, which the tests use; an older retailer text says 2 kHz (that is the MK1 value). The 2500 Hz MK2 carrier, 3000 Hz MK2 CD carrier and side lengths are confirmed from xwax timecoder.c (traktor_mk2_a/b/cd) as vendored in Mixxx. The MK1 control CD carrier is still unknown. Lead-in length is not confirmed.

specs.label: MK1 carrier frequency
specs.notes: Described as two sine waves of 2 kHz; Serato is 1 kHz.

specs.label: MK2 carrier frequency
specs.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions) traktor_mk2_a/traktor_mk2_b, resolution 2500
specs.notes: xwax resolution 2500 for traktor_mk2_a/b (cycles per second at 33 1/3 rpm). The retailer text (PSSL) saying 2 kHz is the MK1 value.

specs.label: MK2 side A timecode length
specs.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions) traktor_mk2_a length 1845000 cycles / 2500 Hz = 738 s

specs.label: MK2 side B timecode length
specs.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions) traktor_mk2_b length 2590000 cycles / 2500 Hz = 1036 s

specs.label: MK2 control CD carrier frequency
specs.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions) traktor_mk2_cd, resolution 3000
specs.notes: MK2 CD code length 4500000 cycles = 25.0 min. The MK1 control CD carrier is not in xwax.

formats.name: Traktor Scratch MK2
formats.notes: Owner format. 2500 Hz carrier (xwax traktor_mk2_a/b, 110-bit code with offset modulation). Side A 12.3 min (1845000 cycles), side B 17.3 min (2590000 cycles).
formats.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions); https://mixxx.org/news/2025-08-27-dvs-internals-pt3/

formats.name: Traktor Scratch MK1
formats.notes: Secondary format (older MK1 vinyl). Absolute and relative modes supported.
formats.source: xwax lib/xwax/timecoder.c as vendored in Mixxx (timecode definitions) traktor_a/traktor_b (resolution 2000); https://djtechtools.com/2009/08/03/timecode-exlplained-basic

formats.name: Traktor Scratch MK2 CD

tests.title: Traktor Scratch MK2 format check (33 1/3)
tests.why: Carrier frequency, quadrature phase, L/R balance and SNR show whether the vinyl, cartridge and input stage deliver a decodable signal.
steps: Clean the record and stylus.
Play the timecode side on a turntable at 33 1/3 rpm, pitch 0.
Run the check for at least 20 s per deck.
equipment: Phono/line input of a DVS interface

tests.title: Traktor Scratch MK2 at 45 rpm
tests.why: Speed tracking at 45 rpm (carrier scales with speed).
steps: Set the deck to 45 rpm and repeat the format check.

tests.title: Traktor Scratch MK1 (secondary) format check (33 1/3)
tests.why: Carrier frequency, quadrature phase, L/R balance and SNR show whether the vinyl, cartridge and input stage deliver a decodable signal.
steps: Clean the record and stylus.
Play the timecode side on a turntable at 33 1/3 rpm, pitch 0.
Run the check for at least 20 s per deck.
equipment: Phono/line input of a DVS interface

tests.title: Traktor Scratch MK1 (secondary) at 45 rpm
tests.why: Speed tracking at 45 rpm (carrier scales with speed).
steps: Set the deck to 45 rpm and repeat the format check.

tests.title: DVS signal: both decks
tests.why: Generic integrity of the sine pair: dropouts, imbalance, noise.
steps: Play control media on each deck for a full minute.
Run DVS signal and read dropouts/level.

tests.title: Vinyl side scan for damage
tests.why: Scratches, warps or wear cause dropouts at a repeatable position on the side.
steps: Play the full timecode side from lead-in to end while the app records.
Note positions of dropouts and compare with visible damage.

tests.title: Cartridge channel separation with control vinyl
tests.why: Channel crosstalk >~ 20 dB destroys quadrature decoding.
steps: Play the timecode side; run the test.

tests.title: Speed accuracy from timecode carrier
tests.why: A turntable running fast/slow shows up as carrier shift; compare against nominal pitch 0 and platter speed.

params.note: reference carrier for the medium in use, see timecode block

steps: Select the medium carrier frequency in the app (MK1 vs MK2).
Run at 33 1/3 and 45 rpm.

tests.title: Timecode calibration in Traktor
tests.why: The Timecode Setup panel measures the signal and sets input gain; it fails on bad signal/wiring.
steps: In Traktor open Preferences > Timecode Setup, pick MK1 or MK2 for each deck.
Start playback of the timecode and press Calibrate; wait until both L and R scopes are a clean circle.
Note the signal quality shown and adjust the input gain/phono-line setting if it fails.
Test Absolute, Relative and Internal modes by loading a track and watching the deck.

tests.title: Traktor install and log scan
tests.why: Looks for crashes and log errors around audio device and timecode errors.
steps: Run the software check.
Open Documents\Native Instruments\Traktor <ver>\Logs for details.

tests.title: Absolute mode and lead-in sanity
tests.why: Absolute mode only works when the needle lands in the timecode area; positions repeat across the lead-in.
steps: Drop the needle at the very start of the side and note Traktor shows a start position.
Drop in the middle: absolute position should match the same groove position each time.
Lift/replace at the end of the side.

tests.title: Record condition
tests.why: Warp, scratches and dust are the usual cause of timecode loss.
steps: Inspect both sides for scratches, warp and dust.
Check the record sits flat on the platter with a slipmat.
Compare two copies if available.
